final_answer: Special relativity establishes that the speed of light (c) is a universal speed limit. When an object approaches c, its relativistic mass increases due to the Lorentz factor (γ = 1 / √(1 - v²/c²)). This means more energy is required to accelerate it, and as v approaches c, γ approaches infinity, requiring infinite energy. Additionally, time dilation occurs: time slows for the moving object relative to a stationary observer, preventing any frame from surpassing c. Causality also preserves: faster-than-light travel would allow events to be observed before they occur, violating physical consistency. Thus, nothing can exceed c.
